title: Comparison configuration
lead: Applied SDK configuration, the reason for each property, and relevant defaults for the selected player versions.

blocks.text: Read the applied settings

After a trial, Applied configuration shows the SDK configuration and source/play calls reconstructed from that trial’s safe settings snapshot. License keys and source addresses are represented by variables. The examples below describe the default HLS startup profile; choose a player in the app to inspect a DASH trial or a declared tuning override.

The reasons below distinguish integration requirements and fixed comparison conditions from measured tuning. A 12-second forward target and 6-second retention are bounded comparison conditions, not proven optimal values or identical memory limits. Web X 10.3.1 does not expose equivalent buffer settings in its native PlayerConfig. Settings left to each SDK can affect the result.

Startup and seek fixes the common fixture to one 360p representation with the same English audio, so initial ABR choices do not make one engine decode lower-quality media. Network change keeps the adaptive ladder. Custom URLs retain their own renditions and SDK quality selection; confirm actual resolution before comparing those timings.
Settings evaluated on the fixed fixture

The retained startup benchmark screened worker and prefetch candidates on the same 360p HLS, then ran fresh confirmation trials. Its selector uses native playing, while the table also retains moving-frame timings. These observations use that benchmark clock; they are not mixed with the playback demo results. Small screening groups and confirmation of only the selected setting do not establish a globally optimal configuration.

Player Web X 10.3.1

For the app-owned fixed 360p HLS source, Web X uses an async createPlayer factory built from the public core bundle and 20 public packages. After measuring that source, open Applied configuration, expand Player Web X, and copy its public imports and complete createPlayer factory, including the ViewMode validation helpers. The example below uses that factory with the actual PlayerConfig and Source API calls. playerKey, mediaUrl, video and container are supplied by the surrounding application.

blocks.text: The compact composition is selected only for the app-owned comparison-360p.m3u8 HLS source. It retains audio/video playback, automatic adaptation, Source controls and ViewMode. CorePlayer supplies Core, EventBus and PlayerApi; the factory adds the 20 packages in its recorded order. TS parsing/transmuxing, AES decryption, subtitles, UI, Analytics and advertising packages are omitted because this controlled source does not require them. This source-specific packaging choice does not establish a speed advantage or an optimal configuration.

Custom HLS URLs and the adaptive source used by Network change keep the complete playerx-hls bundle. DASH uses playerx-dash; DASH support in Web X 10.3.1 is partial. Entering the controlled source address as a custom URL still uses the prebuilt bundle. The app does not infer that an arbitrary HLS URL is safe for the compact composition. Inspect Applied configuration for the bundle and settings actually used by that trial.

Before constructing CorePlayer, the factory checks the public ViewMode package: onAdd must be a function and its dependencies must be exactly core-effects, source-state-atom and source-api-manager. It accepts the package directly or inside one default namespace wrapper, preserving the package object. Deeper or incompatible wrappers fail before construction. If adding a package fails after construction, the async factory awaits player.dispose() before rethrowing; constructorEnd is recorded only after successful factory resolution, including package registration. SDK import starts after the measurement clock; normal licensing behavior is retained.

Native PlayerConfig in 10.3.1 exposes no startup bitrate, buffer threshold, worker toggle or request-concurrency setting used by this adapter. The installed public Streaming implementation initializes forward/backward buffer targets to 12/6 seconds; this adapter does not override those initial targets and retains default WISH adaptation. These are version-specific implementation observations, not additional PlayerConfig controls or measured optima. v8 TweaksConfig names cannot be copied into the native Web X API.
Bitmovin Player 8.283.0

Register the modules before constructing the player. In 8.283.0, the first addModule initializes the module registry, so getModules cannot be used to guard that first registration. Some bundlers wrap a CommonJS module definition in a default namespace. The app unwraps that public definition and passes the original object to addModule; the full code is available in Applied configuration.

blocks.text: The HLS wrapper registers core, EngineBitmovin, RendererMSE, HLS, ABR, MP4 and TS; DASH replaces HLS/TS with XML/DASH. No UI, Analytics or ad module is registered. Startup bitrate stays automatic. The default adaptation logic is DOWNLOAD_PREDICTION (v3), and preload is true for VOD / false for live. The inherited startup_threshold and restart_threshold remain 0.9 seconds: setting forwardduration=12 does not change either threshold. hls_parse_manifest_in_worker remains false. Audio/video codec priorities and platform-specific max_startup_buffer remain at SDK defaults.

blocks.text: Initial quality remains automatic: startLevel is not pinned, abrEwmaDefaultEstimate stays at 500,000 bit/s and testBandwidth stays true. No codec is forced. Player-size and frame-drop quality caps remain false. A configured worker may fall back or be unnecessary for a particular container. DASH is unsupported and is recorded as such, rather than timing a different source.

blocks.text: DASH uses shaka-player.dash-es2021.js. segmentPrefetchLimit is left at its 5.3.3 default of 1 unless an explicit tuning trial overrides it. ABR remains enabled; the 1,000,000 bit/s fallback estimate can be replaced by browser Network Information. Quality is not capped to element or screen size. No transmuxWorkerUrl is set, so worker activation is not established. CODECS in the manifest take precedence over HLS fallback codec strings; no codec is forced by this adapter.
